title: Exact ringed pullback identifies the canonical signed derived tensor comparison
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ and $(\mathcal D,S)$ be ringed sites small relative to a common universe of ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ be a geometric morphism of their sheaf topoi, with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits and a map of commutative ring sheaves $u^{-1}R\to S$. The module pullback $F(M)=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ uses [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; assume $F$ exact. Use the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the actual K-flat derived tensors [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and the canonical left derived pullback $L=Lu^*$ with its resolving-model comparison $e_E:L(q_RE)\cong q_S(FE)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Let $U=D(F)$ be localization of termwise $F$, with factorization $\kappa_E:U(q_RE)\cong q_S(FE)$.

There is a unique natural isomorphism $\eta:L\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ with $\kappa_E\eta_{q_RE}=e_E$ for every flat-term K-flat $E$. It respects all integer shift comparisons and the degree-zero sheaf comparisons. Module pullback preserves flat sheaves and flat-term K-flat complexes [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex].

Transport along $\eta$ the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $\mu_{K,H}:U(K\otimes_R^LH)\cong UK\otimes_S^LUH$. It is the unique natural comparison satisfying, for every resolving pair $E,G$, with $V=T(E,G)$ and the representative isomorphisms $r,r'$,
$$(\kappa_E\otimes\kappa_G)\,\mu_{q_RE,q_RG}\,U(r_{E,G})=r'_{FE,FG}\,q_S(c_{E,G})\,\kappa_V.$$
Here $T$ is signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and $c:FT(E,G)\cong T(FE,FG)$ is the cochain comparison $c_{u;E,G}$ of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence], the total of the normalized ordinary pure-tensor comparison [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]: on local generalized pure tensors it sends $s\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. Its inverse sends $(s\otimes x)\otimes(t\otimes y)$ to $st\otimes(x\otimes y)$. The ordinary comparison and its total respect reassociation and signed interchange [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]; termwise $F$ preserves direct sums and all integer differential, shift and interchange signs.

Let $s_{n,K}:U(K[n])\cong(UK)[n]$, and let $t,\alpha,\sigma$ and $t',\alpha',\sigma'$ be the derived comparisons normalized on total models by $(-1)^{bp}$, unsigned reassociation, and $(-1)^{pq}$, respectively. For arbitrary derived $K,H,N$ and all integers $a,b$, the prescribed comparison satisfies
$$t'_{a,b}(s_{a,K}\otimes s_{b,H})\mu_{K[a],H[b]}=\mu_{K,H}[a+b]s_{a+b,K\otimes^LH}U(t_{a,b}),$$
$$\mu_{H,K}U(\sigma_{K,H})=\sigma'_{UK,UH}\mu_{K,H},$$
$$(1\otimes\mu_{H,N})\mu_{K,H\otimes^LN}U(\alpha_{K,H,N})=\alpha'_{UK,UH,UN}(\mu_{K,H}\otimes1)\mu_{K\otimes^LH,N}.$$
These are equations for the canonical comparison with its specified representative normalization, including when both complexes are unbounded. Under $\eta$, $\mu$ is the normalized comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit] (its representative formula is the displayed one, since $\kappa\eta=e$), so the first equation refines the separate-variable shift equations of that node to the composite signed comparisons $t,t'$.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib isLeftDerivedFunctor_of_inverts to the exact factorization kappa. The left-derived uniqueness isomorphism gives eta with eta_Q(P) followed by kappa_P equal to epsilon_P for every complex P. Transport the exact localization shift structure to L through eta inverse; the factorization equation then proves shift compatibility of epsilon. For uniqueness under resolving normalization, resolve an arbitrary complex by a flat-term K-flat P, cancel kappa_P and use naturality along the inverted resolution map, then the localization object-preimage isomorphism. This also gives the equation on every degree-zero sheaf. This replaces the homotopy-only exact-identification interface while preserving independent derived universes.

Use the canonical shift-unit theorem to obtain the normalized tensor shifts and muL. The existing module adjunction gives all small coproducts and additivity gives preservation of integer multiples. Apply the ringed-topos K-flat pullback theorem for resolving preservation. For a flat M, the complex M[0] has flat terms and is K-flat by derived_tensor_model_closure; its pulled-back degree zero is FM and is flat. Thus all preservation hypotheses of resolving signed coherence hold.

Take the unique normalized natural associator and symmetry over each ring from derived-tensor-additive-constraints. Their components define the required TensorConstraints; the representative equations follow by canceling the representative isomorphisms, and totalModel supplies resolving proofs for both nested totals. Apply resolving-tensor-signed-coherence to eta and muL. Its transportedComparison is the required mu; unfold its components for the transport formula. Expand tensorShift and reassociate to identify its simultaneous-shift formula. The symmetry and reassociation equations are its remaining conclusions.
